title: Bhumi Pednekar Walks for Nazranaa at New York Fashion Week in Maroon Lehenga
excerpt: The Bollywood actor made her runway debut at NYFW as the showstopper for Nazranaa's Samskriti 2.0 collection, a line inspired by Indian temple architecture and craft traditions.
body:
• Bollywood actor Bhumi Pednekar made her New York Fashion Week runway debut as the showstopper for Nazranaa's Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Samskriti 2.0.
  • Pednekar wore a royal maroon velvet lehenga inspired by the architecture of the Belur Math Shri Ramakrishna Temple in West Bengal, with gold zari work, hand embroidery, a swan motif and a cape-style dupatta.
  • The collection is the follow-up to Nazranaa's 2025 Samskriti line, which turned sacred texts and temple art into wearable couture.
  • Nazranaa, founded in 2012 in New Jersey, describes itself as the largest South Asian bridal boutique in the US.

New York Fashion Week has a new showstopper. Bollywood actor Bhumi Pednekar closed the runway for Nazranaa on the international stage this week, unveiling the New Jersey-based label's Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Samskriti 2.0, in a regal maroon velvet lehenga. The appearance marks Pednekar's debut walk at NYFW.

The lehenga drew directly on the architecture of the Belur Math Shri Ramakrishna Temple in West Bengal. According to coverage of the show, the garment translated the temple's symmetry, arched openings and carved detailing into couture: deep maroon velvet set against gold zari work and hand embroidery, with a swan design worked into the skirt and a dupatta styled like a cape. The jewel-like color became the backdrop for intricate stonework and beadwork, merging Indian craft traditions with contemporary tailoring.

A collection built on heritage

Nazranaa's Samskriti line is, at its core, an argument that couture can carry scripture and architecture. The 2.0 collection leans on themes of Indian architecture, spirituality and intellectual tradition — a step beyond bridal dressing into narrative fashion.

The concept has a lineage. When the label launched the original Samskriti collection at NYFW last year, the showstopper lehenga translated an idea attributed to Maharishi Valmiki into cloth: the 24-syllable Gayatri Mantra woven through the Ramayana, with each thousandth verse opening on the next syllable. The garment carried 24 panels, each opening with a syllable of the mantra, followed by the corresponding verse and chapter, and each panel was hand-painted with the story of that chapter, while the dupatta depicted the sage himself writing the scripture.

"Samskriti is our humble effort to give credit to works of art like this and to honor our ancestors through couture."

— Shashank Gupta, co-founder, Nazranaa

That 18-piece collection of sherwanis and lehengas treated garments as canvases of storytelling. This year's edition keeps the storytelling but shifts the source material from sacred text to sacred architecture.

Who is behind the label

Nazranaa was founded in 2012 by Shashank Gupta and Shivangi Gupta Singh, and has grown from a New Jersey bridal boutique into what the brand calls the largest South Asian bridal boutique in the US, built on bespoke and custom-made bridalwear. A New York Fashion Week showcase is a different kind of credential — it places an Indian-American bridal house on the same calendar as the industry's global names.

The front row reflected the label's crossover audience. Content creator Apoorva, known as Rebel Kid, attended her first-ever NYFW show in Nazranaa, styled head to toe in the brand — a shimmery embellished corset-style top paired with a flowing skirt and a bindi. Apoorva recently moved to New York to pursue an MBA at NYU Stern, and documented the evening against the Manhattan skyline with the caption, "my first ever NYFW show for and in @nazranaa," according to reports.

Why it matters

The presence of a Bollywood star closing for an Indian-American label at NYFW lands at a moment when South Asian fashion is moving from the margins of Western runways to their center. Pednekar has walked ramps in India before — she has been a showstopper at India Couture Week for designers like Varun Bahl — but a New York debut in a garment rooted in Bengali temple architecture sends a different signal: Indian craft presented not as costume or inspiration, but as couture in its own right.

For brides watching the trend cycle, the details matter too. Fashion writers covering the show noted that the maroon palette, the cape-like dupatta and the architectural embroidery read as a 2026 bridal direction — traditional forms reworked with a modern silhouette.

What's next

Nazranaa's new collection will be available through the label's website, nazranaanj.com. The label has not yet announced whether it will expand its NYFW presence beyond the annual showcase. For Pednekar, the walk adds fashion-week credentials to a year that has already kept her busy on screen — and puts a Maroon velvet lehenga firmly on the season's mood board.
image_caption: Bhumi Pednekar walks the runway in a maroon velvet lehenga. She closed the show as the showstopper for Nazranaa's Samskriti 2.0 collection at New York Fashion Week.
nri_angle: A New Jersey Indian-American bridal house closing NYFW with a Bollywood star shows how diaspora fashion businesses are carrying Indian craft onto the global runway in their own right.
author: Diaspora Desk
